title: Spring Data JPA
description: Learn Spring Data JPA as the Spring repository abstraction built on top of JPA, reaching professional competency in designing repository layers, querying data cleanly, testing persistence behavior, and diagnosing performance problems without treating repository interfaces as magic.

nodes.label: Prerequisite Review & Abstraction Stack
nodes.description: Confirm readiness in ORM/JPA/Hibernate fundamentals and Spring Boot basics, then map the layered relationship between Spring Data JPA, JPA, Hibernate, JDBC, and the database so each layer's responsibility stays distinct.

nodes.description: Add the Spring Data JPA starter and the correct database driver, configure a datasource with externalized credentials, and ensure entities and repositories live where Spring Boot's scanning can discover them.

nodes.label: Repository Concept & Hierarchy
nodes.description: Understand why the repository abstraction exists and what belongs in it versus the service layer, then trace the Repository/CrudRepository/PagingAndSortingRepository/JpaRepository interface hierarchy to explain why JpaRepository is the common practical choice.

nodes.label: Generics, Inherited CRUD & Return Types
nodes.description: Declare JpaRepository<Entity, Id> with correct generic types, use inherited save/findById/findAll/delete/exists/count methods with an accurate mental model of entity lifecycle, and choose appropriate return shapes (Optional, List, Page, Slice, projection) based on semantics.

nodes.label: Derived Query Fundamentals & Keywords
nodes.description: Write queries derived from method names using comparison, string, boolean/null, and collection keywords, combine conditions with And/Or, and traverse nested mapped properties, while recognizing when a derived name becomes too unwieldy to stay readable.

nodes.label: Ordering, Limiting & Sorting
nodes.description: Apply static ordering in derived method names, limit results with First/Top keywords, handle null/optional results and parameters correctly, and use a dynamic Sort parameter instead of multiplying near-identical repository methods.

nodes.label: Pagination: Pageable, Page & Slice
nodes.description: Replace unbounded result loading with Pageable-driven paging, and choose deliberately between Page (with total counts) and Slice (cheaper has-next-only paging) based on what the caller actually needs.

nodes.description: Write explicit @Query methods in JPQL and native SQL when derived names fall short, bind parameters safely without string concatenation, and implement @Modifying update/delete queries with correct transaction boundaries and persistence-context awareness.

nodes.description: Return narrower interface-based or DTO/record projections instead of full entities when only a subset of fields is needed, and understand when projections earn their complexity over returning the entity directly.

nodes.description: Compose JpaSpecificationExecutor Specifications to handle search forms with many optional filters instead of writing a combinatorial explosion of repository methods, and validate sort/filter/page inputs so user-controlled search endpoints stay safe.

nodes.label: Transactions & Layer Boundaries
nodes.description: Place @Transactional at the service layer to group multiple repository calls into one unit of work, use readOnly and rollback semantics correctly, and keep business logic out of repositories while avoiding controller-to-repository shortcuts.

nodes.description: Query mapped relationships through derived properties, JPQL joins, and Specifications, recognize the N+1 query problem and detect it with SQL logging, and correct fetch behavior deliberately with fetch joins or @EntityGraph rather than switching everything to eager loading.

nodes.description: Translate low-level persistence exceptions into appropriate service/API responses instead of leaking them, and choose the right test type — @DataJpaTest for real repository/query behavior versus Mockito-mocked repositories for service logic, backed by production-like database testing where behavior matters.

nodes.description: Recognize common Spring Data JPA performance problems — N+1, missing pagination, expensive counts, missing indexes — by measuring with SQL logs and query plans rather than judging by Java method appearance, and debug failures layer by layer from controller down through JDBC.

nodes.description: Keep persistence entities out of the public API contract, validate at every appropriate boundary, bound user-controlled query parameters like page size and sort fields, and avoid logging sensitive data or entire entities in production.
